name: Glass Beach
description: A shore of smooth, colorful sea glass
adjustment: Replace the oversized glossy sea-glass boulders at the left and right edges and bottom corners with small ordinary smooth sea-glass pebbles. Every colored sea-glass piece should be about 15–35px long on a 1536px canvas, at most 2–2.3% of the canvas width, much smaller than the creature's head. Retain their aqua, mint, amber and lavender colors in sparse low clusters or patches along the same edges; use a few dozen simple pebbles, not noisy hundreds of detailed beads. Restore sand and keep the normal large gray coastal rocks/cliffs, ocean, shoreline and horizon unchanged. Do not simply shrink the whole scene.
prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Image 1 is the EXACT SQUARE BACKGROUND TO EDIT. Image 2 is a cropped IN-GAME SCALE GUIDE with a creature temporarily overlaid; it is NOT the output composition. Use its creature only as a size reference. The creature occupies about 22% of the background width including its tail.
Make ONLY the requested prop-size corrections to Image 1. Preserve the existing scene, camera, horizon, framing, large landscape shapes, colors, lighting, thick near-black cartoon outlines and simple cel shading. Do not zoom out, shrink the entire image, rearrange the environment or add new motifs. Cleanly repaint the areas exposed by shrinking the props in the same existing ground/water/rock style. Tiny props can have proportionately thinner but still clear black strokes, with fewer interior marks.
The finished output must be the same full square background as Image 1, target 1536×1536, opaque, edge to edge. DO NOT draw or bake in the creature, people, UI, labels, annotations, a measuring guide, a border or a comparison layout. Keep the low central standing area clear and preserve its ground at x50%, y93%.

STRICT VISUAL SCALE CHECK: ordinary small props should be comparable to or smaller than ONE EYE of the creature in Image 2, far smaller than its head. Do not settle for making them only a little smaller: the requested reduction is substantial. Lily pads and total mushroom heights follow their stated limits; coin marks should be much smaller still. The creature is a ruler only and must not appear in the output.

SPECIFIC CORRECTION: Second precision pass: the colored sea-glass pieces in Image 1 are STILL too big and read as rocks. Shrink EVERY mint, aqua, purple and amber glass pebble at the sides and bottom corners to 20–25% of its CURRENT width and height. The largest must be only 20–30px long on a 1536px canvas, most 10–20px: no bigger than the smallest dark specks/pebbles already scattered on the sand, and noticeably smaller than one creature eye in Image 2. Preserve sparse clusters of these TINY colored pebbles near the same edges; fill the vacated areas with sand. No large shiny glass chunks may remain anywhere, including the clipped bottom corners. Keep the natural large tan/gray cliffs and rocks, plants, beach, water and exact viewpoint unchanged. Output only the square background.

name: Dragon's Hoard
description: A vast cavern heaped with gold and jewels
adjustment: Make the loose gold coins on the foreground floor small coin-sized details, about 15–20% of their present diameter, generally 8–16px across on a 1536px canvas. Reduce the huge individual red/blue/green cut gemstones at the foreground sides to about 15–20% of their present dimensions, typically 20–40px and max 50px. Preserve the overall large gold-heap silhouettes and existing treasure chests, but render the heaps as broad gold color masses with only sparse tiny coin marks so individual coins are not giant disks. Fill former gem footprints with matching gold/smooth cave floor. Keep cavern, lighting, layout and center open.
